notes.summary: Independent canonical envelope reconstruction on every excellent reduced germ; uniform convergence remains the decisive condition.
notes.detailedSummary: Proves all-support raw C/D equality, every-degree canonical primary profiles and convergence, exact continuity criterion, fixed-obstacle FG equivalence, gauges, conditional full-fibre conductor descent and geometric curve clipping, relative only to qualified G331.
notes.text:
Independent reconstruction of the canonical envelope argument, relative to the ENTIRE qualified G331. All its source annotations, model restrictions and reading limits remain attached. Let R be excellent local, reduce nilpotents, fix a proper primary ideal a, and write X=V_a(R), C=C_geom and D=D_geom. Every prime support remains. G331 grants the independently defined actual negative effective real Cartier core with nonnegative degree on EVERY contracted integral curve on directed ACTUAL primary blowups, its comparison with ideal C/D, and positive full-fibre descent. It grants no envelope theorem.

For finite continuous signed f set A_0=R and A_m={g in R: v(g)+m f(v)>=0 for every v in X}. If M=max(0,-min f), then a^N subset A_m for positive N>=mM. The ultrametric inequality and v(R)>=0 prove idealness. A negative obstacle value excludes every unit, so A_m is proper primary; if f>=0 everywhere A_m=R. Multiplicativity gives A_m A_n subset A_(m+n). In a monic ideal-integrality equation for g, v(g)<v(A_m) makes the leading term uniquely least and finite, a contradiction. Thus A_m is integrally closed. Define h_m=-v(A_m)/m. Its primary Cartier presentation is negative effective and relatively ample; units give zero. Therefore h_m belongs to the independently geometric C and h_m<=f.

Let p(f)=sup{u in D:u<=f}, initially only a pointwise function. It equals sup of rational primary/unit profiles below f and equals sup_m h_m. A rational competitor -v(I)/r<=f has I subset A_r. Conversely every C competitor is uniformly approximable by rational profiles; subtract a sufficiently small positive rational a-constant, realized by multiplying powered ideals, to obtain competitors converging from below. For u=inf_i g_i<=f in an actual decreasing C-net, the open sets {g_i<f+epsilon} cover compact X and are directed under inclusion. One index works everywhere. Then g_i-epsilon is a C competitor below f and u<=p_C(f)+epsilon. This proves p_D=p_C, including bottom and partial poles. No supremum positivity is inferred here.

Set M_1=||v(A_1)|| and H_N=max_(1<=r<=N)h_r in C. For m=kr+s, 0<=s<r, A_r^k A_1^s subset A_m gives h_m>=(kr/m)h_r-sM_1/m>=h_r-rM_1/m because h_r<=0. Hence H_N-NM_1/m<=h_m<=p. Every degree h_m converges pointwise to finite p. Since p is a supremum of continuous functions, it is lower semicontinuous. It is continuous iff H_N converges uniformly iff h_m converges uniformly: continuity gives the increasing compact strict-error cover for H_N; the displayed bound transfers uniform convergence to all degrees; the converse follows from uniform limits. When continuous, p belongs to closed geometric C and is the greatest D minorant. This is the precise missing general regularity step.

Subtracting an epsilon a-constant from a D competitor below f makes it a competitor below g whenever f<=g+epsilon. Reversing f and g proves ||p(f)-p(g)||<=||f-g||. In particular uniform obstacle density transfers CE once envelopes for the dense family are actually positive and continuous.

The fixed-obstacle finite-generation equivalence in current413 is also valid at its stated scope. If the canonical algebra is generated by homogeneous g_i t^(d_i), let L be divisible by all d_i and J=(g_i^(L/d_i)). Any degree-m expression has value at least m min_i v(g_i)/d_i. Pure powers attain this bound in degree L, so p=h_L=-v(J)/L=max_(r<=max d_i)h_r. J is primary or unit: its radical contains A_1, and the proper case lies in m. The residue bound gives uniform error <=(max d_i)M_1/m. Conversely, if p=-v(J)/q, its defining inequalities imply A_m={g:g^q in integral-closure(J^m)}. The centred rank-one DVR criterion is applied to each positive-dimensional minimal-component domain and then combined by SH1.1.5 and6.8.3--4. Every such DVR normalizes into X. Monic equations prove the reverse inequalities on every other support. A zero-dimensional minimal component in a reduced local positive-dimensional ring would make m minimal and force dimension zero, so none is lost.

To prove finiteness without assuming a section algebra is finitely generated, put B=R[Jt^q]. A primary J contains a regular element. B is reduced excellent with total quotient product K_j(t^q). Excellent/Nagata finiteness of integral closure in the finite product K_j(t), also when inseparable, supplies a finite B-module. An equation for g^q over J^m, multiplied by the requisite powers of t^(mq), makes g^q t^(mq) integral over B, then gt^m integral by its qth-power equation. The canonical algebra is a B-submodule of this finite module and hence is finite. The unit case is R[t]. A finite maximum of rational profiles is rational by summing suitable powers. This proves canonical FG iff rational attainment iff finite canonical-max attainment, and says nothing about FG density.

For a signed exceptional integral Cartier obstacle f_D on a normal primary model, pass to its finite normalization Y. The equality A_m=H^0(Y,O(mD)) intersect R follows from exceptional height-one order tests and the normal height-one intersection criterion. At other height-one primes g is regular and D vanishes. Conversely a section is pulled to the valuation ring of Frac(R/p) at each support p: its generic point is outside the exceptional fibre, so the invertible lattice has its nonzero generic trivialization and gives v(g)>=-m f_D(v). No fraction field of R is mapped through nonzero p. This proves the section formula, not general FG.

For another primary b let d(v)=v(b)>0 and T(v)=v/d(v). Transport f by f_b(Tv)=f(v)/d(v). All defining inequalities divide by d, so every A_m and its algebra are literally unchanged; h_m and p divide by d. This gives the exact gauge cocycle and transports uniform convergence since d and 1/d are bounded. For normalization S, surjective restriction gives A_m^R=A_m^S intersect R. A continuous source envelope descends to the downstairs envelope if it is constant on EVERY actual fibre, including the infinite-conductor quotient fibres, by G331's positive C descent and pullback of D competitors. Obstacle compatibility alone does not prove this constancy. A decreasing family of continuous obstacles with C envelopes has the D envelope equal to the infimum of those envelopes: it is an actual decreasing C-net, lies below the limiting obstacle, and dominates every competitor.

On an excellent reduced curve the normalization centres are DVRs. A regular conductor element has finite positive order at every branch, so normalized boundary fibres are singletons. Every real nonpositive slope is an actual Cartier evaluation on a DVR, with no contracted-curve test. Semilocal gluing and G331 positive descent give the finite nonpositive orthant C; coordinate truncations give the extended orthant D. The geometric envelope is min(f,0), exactly the ideal envelope. Literal classical/CLD multibranch radial extensions remain distinct, retaining the mixed-zero obstruction. A DVR obstacle -alpha, alpha irrational positive, has a real Cartier continuous envelope but A_m=(x^ceil(m alpha)) is not FG, since finite homogeneous generation would force a rational minimum order/degree slope. Non-FG is not a CE failure. Zero-dimensional reduction has empty boundary; nilpotents are invisible.

These arguments reconstruct the used current413 canonical results without using its verdict or compiler record as a theorem. Complete immediate SH units and both formula pages were freshly read/viewed; their named deeper foundations retain the disclosed limits. Artifacts: n1.txt, expanded n1.tex, P12.3-surface-envelopes.tex, proof-companion.md. Rerun: python build_delivery.py; python check_delivery.py. Execution is serialization evidence only.

notes.summary: Exact smooth, quotient, coefficient-field and Frobenius-root current413 results independently reconstructed at their stated scopes.
notes.detailedSummary: Reconstructs BFJ real-parameter/all-support model estimate only at published char-zero smooth hypotheses, full orbit quotient descent, every-degree separable coefficient descent, and unique-lift root transport. Characteristic-p source CE is not inferred from BFJ.
notes.text:
Independent reconstruction of current413's smooth, quotient, coefficient-field and root arguments. Supports are qualified G331 and own n1; current413 is DATA. The published BFJ application is ONLY a smooth affine CLOSED germ over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, dimension>=2. DVR and empty cases are n1. The complete immediate setting, modification/retraction chain1.10--1.15,2.1--2.8,3.1--3.14 and3.15--3.25, including the entire3.18 proof, were freshly read. Hironaka smooth characteristic-zero principalization, smooth multiplier subadditivity, thinness and smooth Izumi are qualified deeper foundations, not characteristic-free inputs.

For a model obstacle F=F composed with r_pi0 let M=max(0,-min F). Nef divisors below its coefficients form a max-directed family after adjoining the barrier -M. Their coefficient supremum W lies in the weak closed nef cone and -M<=W<=0. BFJ3.11 supplies substantive continuity on every CLOSED simplex, and the full function H(v)=inf_pi H(r_pi v). Divisorial density and refinements of pi0 give H<=F on every support. G331's exact BFJ comparison gives every D competitor below H, so H is the raw envelope. Canonical B_m=L-infinity(mW)=L-infinity(mZ(F)) contains a primary power. To identify it with n1's all-support A_m, test (g)+mhat^N with N>=mM: its divisorial inequalities extend by closed-simplex continuity and cofinal retractions, and v(g)>=v((g)+mhat^N). Completion and exact primary contraction in G331 identify B_m with A_m in the local ring.

If W=0, F>=0 by density and the envelope is zero. Otherwise BFJ3.14 makes H strictly negative. Thinness is bounded only on the fixed compact complex; choose C>0 with A<=-CW there. The complete3.18 proof yields W_t<=W<=(1-C/t)W_(t-C) for real t>C: part(i) applies to real scalar multiples, and part(ii) is the same defining fixed-complex inequality for real t. Put t=m+C to obtain (1+C/m)W<=W_m<=W. Closed simplices and all retraction infima give 0<=H-h_m<=CM/m on EVERY support. Thus H belongs to continuous geometric C. Signed model functions are uniformly dense by the lattice ideal identities and BFJ1.14--1.15. N1's Lipschitz estimate gives CE for every continuous signed obstacle at exactly these hypotheses. No FG is used.

For a finite faithful group G acting locally on such a smooth S with finite excellent R=S^G, R is normal and Frac(S)^G=Frac(R), by orbit denominator products. The fixed-field degree proof is elementary: distinct automorphisms are linearly independent as functions, by subtracting a shortest relation evaluated at ax from one evaluated at x; an invertible evaluation matrix gives a basis over the fixed field and degree |G|. Orbit polynomials prove Galoisness. G331's normal-target coefficient trace has full fibre support and is the orbit measure sum_sigma delta_(w composed with sigma), even at nonzero supports. Hence every restriction fibre is a full G-orbit. The source greatest minorant for a pulled obstacle is invariant by uniqueness, thus positively descends through EVERY fibre and is the target greatest minorant. If B_m is its stable canonical ideal, the coefficients J_m of product_sigma(sum_i T_i sigma(s_i)), for finite R-module generators s_i, lie in normal R and satisfy v(J_m)=|G| w(B_m) on every support. They are actual unit-or-primary ideals by G331. Their profiles descend the source approximants exactly.

For fixed signed primary/model obstacles with source error E/m, J_m subset A_(dm)^R, d=|G|. For k>=2d, let m=floor(k/d), r=dm. Grading with A_1^(k-r) gives 0<=p_R-h_k^R<=E/floor(k/d)+dM_1/k<=(2dE+dM_1)/k. This is the precise conditional residue estimate, not same-degree contraction or a general finite-map envelope formula.

The separable coefficient extension argument is valid for a geometrically integral, geometrically normal positive-dimensional normal local domain R essentially of finite type over k with residue field EXACTLY k. For finite Galois E/k, R_E=R tensor E is finite free and local since its closed fibre is the field E; the union R_s over k^s is the corresponding Noetherian excellent normal local ring. Compatible semivaluations on its finite stages define all semivaluations on the union, so X_s=lim_E X_E and restriction is compact surjective. At each finite stage G331's full-fibre trace and the fixed-field proof above give full Galois orbits. For two points in an infinite fibre, the sets of gamma in Gal(k^s/k) matching their E-restrictions are nonempty clopen with the finite-intersection property. Profinite compactness gives one gamma matching every coordinate. Thus full infinite fibres are orbits, without extending through an original fraction field across support.

Every Galois-stable ideal descends without division by group order. In a finite Galois E/k choose basis e_j and trace-dual c_i. Nondegeneracy follows from the invertible embedding matrix M: its trace Gram matrix is M^t M and determinant (det M)^2 is nonzero, including in characteristic dividing |G|. If s=sum r_j e_j is in a stable ideal, sum_sigma sigma(c_i s)=r_i is in its contraction. This proves the ideal is the extension of its contraction. At the infinite stage choose a finite Galois field containing finitely many ideal generators; faithful flat contraction and extension of finite-field automorphisms make that finite ideal stable, so it descends too. Canonical ideals B_m for a pulled obstacle are stable and contract to A_m. Therefore B_m=A_m R_s in EVERY degree, their profiles and raw envelopes pull back exactly, and uniform errors are unchanged. Continuity is equivalent by the compact quotient. FG equivalence follows by faithfully flat detection of degree-generation multiplication maps. For invariant C, approximate by a rational primary profile at a finite stage and replace its ideal by the sum of its Galois translates; its maximum profile stays within the same uniform error and descends by trace-dual extraction. No arbitrary invariant infinite D descent is claimed.

In characteristic zero k^s is algebraically closed. Finite linear smooth quotients at the rational origin over any characteristic-zero k satisfy the required geometric hypotheses after every field extension: polynomial invariants commute with extension degree by degree; orbit polynomials give a finite invariant coefficient algebra and a finite smooth cover; their nonleading coefficients vanish at the origin and force its fibre to have the unique origin; invariant fractions and integral closure prove normality after extension. The smooth quotient result applies only over k^s, and the every-degree identity descends it over k with unchanged model error constants. This includes k[a,b,c,z]/(ac-b^2) at the origin, char(k)=0, a=x^2,b=xy,c=y^2, with its normal nonisolated singular locus (a,b,c). It does not prove positive-characteristic regular source CE.

For an injective finite local excellent reduced characteristic-p extension R subset S with S^q subset R, q=p^e, every semivaluation has the unique lift w(s)=v(s^q)/q. Frobenius addition/multiplication proves the axioms, powers determine every support, and aS normalization proves centredness; the coordinate formulas prove a homeomorphism. For I=(s_i) primary or unit, J=(s_i^q) in R obeys v(J)=q w(I). If I contains (aS)^N, raise each actual expression x=sum s_i u_i, x in a^N, to obtain x^q in J; thus J is primary, and raising a unit expression gives the unit case. Rational density identifies C isometrically; actual decreasing nets identify D. Hence ALL pointwise raw envelopes commute, and CE is equivalent. Canonical contraction is A_m=B_m intersect R and J_m subset A_(qm), giving the conditional rate (2qE+qM_1)/k for k>=2q by the same residue argument. Same-degree scalar extension is not asserted.

If S is a Noetherian local union of finite local root subextensions and its maximal ideal/gauge are extended, each element has some p-power in R. Common exponents prove the coordinate formula, and each finitely generated ideal plus finitely many primary-containment coefficients has one common exponent. The same primary-profile argument identifies C,D and envelopes, but supplies no global rate when exponents are unbounded. Finite purely inseparable extensions of normal domains satisfy S^q subset R by normality and a field exponent. Geometrically integral/normal rational finite-type germs tensor k^perf meet the union hypotheses by Frobenius on their finitely many tensor coefficients. Combining separable closure and perfection reduces their compatible obstacle problem to algebraic closure, without supplying characteristic-p CE there. Mixed characteristic has no such formula.

No literal mathematical correction to these current413 scoped proofs was needed. The real-parameter BFJ step and support-quotient trace are essential, and were checked rather than inferred from old verdicts. Its finite diagnostics and compilation remain observations. Historical recursive audit is not inherited from retained text. Artifacts: n2.txt, distinct expanded n2.tex, source-application-reading-ledger.md and proof-companion.md. Rerun: python build_delivery.py; python check_delivery.py.

notes.summary: New CE theorem for every excellent normal local surface, arbitrary residue field and positive or mixed characteristic.
notes.detailedSummary: Proves actual regular primary refinements using exact two-dimensional Lipman resolution and a section/Rees presentation; solves the finite nef degree maximum; controls every primary-ideal competitor on every support. Uniform density gives every continuous signed obstacle and uniform all-degree canonical convergence. Higher dimension and unrestricted nonnormal conductor descent remain open.
notes.text:
NEW scoped theorem: every excellent normal local domain R of dimension TWO, in arbitrary equal or mixed characteristic and with arbitrary residue field, has a greatest continuous independently geometric C/D envelope for EVERY finite continuous signed obstacle on every primary section. The proof uses qualified G331 and own n1, and a dimension-specific published surface resolution theorem at its actual hypotheses. It does not assume higher-dimensional resolution, algebraizability, F-finiteness, CM or Q-Gorenstein hypotheses for arbitrary original R. It includes genuinely positive-characteristic and mixed-characteristic regular source CE in dimension two.

Step 1: actual regular primary models, proved rather than presumed cofinal. Given finitely many primary ideals, INCLUDE the gauge ideal a in this list and begin with their product blowup, which dominates their individual actual blowups by G331. Normalize it finitely by excellence. This is a normal projective integral surface, an isomorphism on U=Spec(R) minus the closed point; U is regular since R is normal of dimension two. Its singular locus is finite: excellence makes the regular locus open, normality gives regularity in codimension one, and a Noetherian closed zero-dimensional subset is finite. Every singular local completion is normal by excellence. Thus the exact condition(4) of Stacks54.14.5/Lipman holds. Its complete immediate proof, together with54.14.3--4 in the entire0BGJ unit, was read. It produces a regular resolution by finitely many normalized blowups. In that proof the local centres resolving this surface are its singular closed points, all over the marked point. Consequently the final regular surface Y is projective and unchanged on U. No analogous result in larger dimension is used.

Y carries an actual effective exceptional integral divisor E with O(-E) relatively ample and with positive coefficient on every exceptional component. On the initial normalized primary blowup the pullback tautological primary divisor is effective and its negative is ample, including under finite normalization. Each subsequent normalized blowup has its effective tautological divisor with relatively ample negative. Inductively combine this negative with a sufficiently large positive multiple of the pullback of the preceding negative ample divisor. Stacks29.38.7--8, whose whole immediate proofs were read, give ampleness of this combination. Pullbacks of effective Cartier divisors are effective here because every modification is birational integral and is generically outside their support. The initial primary divisor vanishes on the whole closed fibre; its pullback has positive order at every final exceptional component. Keeping it with positive multiplicity makes E have the asserted full support. One can add another positive multiple of it without spoiling ampleness, since its negative is generated by the original primary ideal. This also proves a nonempty exceptional fibre, even if R is regular, by including a proper primary blowup at the start.

Here is a full primary presentation argument, to ensure positivity takes place on an ACTUAL primary model. By proper birational normal-target descent, H^0(Y,O_Y)=R (Stacks37.53.6, complete proof read); alternatively proper finiteness plus normal integral closure gives the same statement. L=O(-E) is ample on Y because the base is affine. Choose finitely many sections s_i of powers of L whose nonvanishing loci Y_(s_i) are affine and cover Y. Make their degrees equal by powers, say n. Each affine Y_(s_i) is of finite type over R; choose finitely many R-algebra generators for its coordinate ring. The ample-section localization identity, proved in Stacks28.27.11, writes each generator as t/s_i^k with t a section of L^(nk). Choose a common K for all these exponents; the sections s_i^K and t s_i^(K-k) of L^(nK) yield a projective-space map. In the s_i^K chart their ratios contain all chosen affine generators, so Y_(s_i) maps as a closed subscheme of that affine chart. These charts cover the image; the map is an immersion. Y is proper over R and projective space is separated, so the immersion is proper and hence a closed immersion.

All the selected sections belong to R because L^(nK) subset O_Y. Let J be their ideal in R. They generate L^(nK), so J O_Y=L^(nK). The ideal is proper: a unit would be a section vanishing on the nonempty E. Off the marked point L is canonically O and generation shows J is the unit ideal. Thus J is proper primary. The projective-space map factors through Bl_J(R), since J O_Y is invertible. This blowup is the integral scheme Proj(R[Jt]) inside the same projective space. The factor is a closed immersion containing its generic point and indeed its dense U. A closed subscheme of an integral reduced scheme containing a dense open must have zero defining ideal. Hence Y IS Bl_J(R). This proves precisely the regular primary refinements needed for finitely many ideal functions; no arbitrary-model cofinality is assumed. The finite section-generation/localization units used here were read with their whole immediate proofs.

Step 2: the finite degree problem. Write the exceptional curves of Y as E_1,...,E_r. Y is regular, so these integral Weil divisors are actual effective Cartier divisors (regular Noetherian local rings are factorial). No SNC or residue-field perfection is required. Write a O_Y=O(-E_a), E_a=sum a_i E_i, a_i positive integers, and let a signed model obstacle be f_D, D=sum d_i E_i. Every finite real signed sum of primary gauges is of this form on the regular primary refinement above.

Define Q_ij=deg_(E_i) O(E_j), with degree over the residue field of R. For i!=j this is nonnegative: restriction gives an effective finite zero divisor, and its degree is the sum of local intersection lengths times residue degrees. The same length O_(Y,x)/(f_i,f_j) computes Q_ji, so Q is symmetric. Nonzero sections of any line bundle on a proper integral curve have nonnegative degree by the effective zero-divisor exact sequence. These arguments apply to nonsmooth integral curves and imperfect residue fields. All contracted proper integral curves on Y are among the E_i. Thus an exceptional real divisor sum z_i E_i is curve-nef exactly when Qz>=0.

Put c_i=min(d_i,0). The feasible vectors are z<=c and Qz>=0. They are nonempty: if M is any nonnegative number with f_D>=-M on X, the divisor -M E_a is a negative effective nef barrier, since -E_a is a pullback of the generated primary tautological bundle. Its coefficient vector b_i=-M a_i satisfies b<=c. Coefficientwise maximum preserves feasibility: at coordinate i choose whichever input has its ith coordinate equal to the maximum; the diagonal contribution is unchanged and every off-diagonal contribution increases because Q_ij>=0. The subset b<=z<=c, Qz>=0 is compact. Maximize each of its finitely many coordinates and then take the finite coordinatewise maximum of these maximizers. The result z* is feasible and dominates the whole subset. Any original feasible z has max(z,b) in that subset, so z* is the GREATEST feasible vector of the entire problem.

Z*=sum z_i* E_i is an actual negative effective finite REAL Cartier presentation and has nonnegative degree on EVERY contracted integral curve. Y is an ACTUAL primary blowup by Step1. Therefore its evaluation H=f_(Z*) belongs to G331's independent geometric core, hence continuous C. Coefficientwise Z*<=D implies H<=f_D on EVERY support by actual Cartier effectivity. In particular this is actual geometric positivity, established before any envelope comparison.

Step 3: every competitor is controlled. Let q=-v(I)/s be a rational primary profile below f_D, s a positive integer. On Y form F_I=sum ord_(E_i)(I) E_i, an actual effective Cartier divisor. Every generator of I is a global section of O(-F_I): its height-one orders have the required lower bounds on the exceptional curves, and are nonnegative at horizontal primes; normal height-one intersection gives regularity after dividing by the Cartier generator. At the generic point of any E_i, some ideal generator attains ord_(E_i)(I). Its resulting section of O(-F_I)|_(E_i) is nonzero. Hence deg_(E_i) O(-F_I)>=0 for EVERY i, by the curve argument above. Consequently A=-F_I/s has Q-coefficients>=0 and is nonpositive.

The normalized divisorial points v_i=ord_(E_i)/a_i lie in X. Testing q<=f_D there gives A_i<=d_i, so A is feasible and A<=Z*. Moreover I O_Y subset O(-F_I) gives q(v)<=f_A(v) on every semivaluation, including nonzero support. To see this without an illicit fraction-field extension, pull both sheaves to the valuation ring of Frac(R/p), where p is that support. Properness gives its centre on Y; its generic point lies over U. The exceptional invertible lattice has a nonzero generic trivialization. Its local generator b and every ideal generator g have g/b regular at the centre, so v(g)>=v(b); a primary generator has finite value, and generators killed by p have infinite value and satisfy the same inequality. Thus q<=f_A<=H EVERYWHERE. The unit case is identical with F_I=0 when zero is a competitor.

N1 identifies the raw D envelope with the supremum of these rational competitors. It follows p(f_D)<=H. The reverse follows because H itself is a C competitor. Hence p(f_D)=H is the greatest C/D minorant, with actual core positivity. This is not norm averaging, a trace of a greatest minorant, or a claim that positivity follows from a raw supremum. No competing-model cofinality or arbitrary nef b-divisor pushforward is needed: the explicit ideal-section argument controls all competitors.

Step 4: all continuous obstacles and regularity. The signed real span of primary profiles is uniformly dense in C(X,R). For clarity the ideal identity proving the lattice condition is min(v(I)-v(J),v(K)-v(H))=v(IH+KJ)-v(JH), after common denominators; the span contains constants through v(a)=1. The truncated profiles v((g)+a^N)=min(v(g),N) separate every pair of semivaluations, including different supports. The compact lattice Stone-Weierstrass argument gives density, as also granted and proved in G331. Choose signed model f_j uniformly converging to f. Their envelopes H_j above are in C. N1's raw Lipschitz estimate makes H_j uniformly Cauchy with limit p(f); closedness of C proves p(f) continuous and geometrically positive. Every canonical degree converges uniformly by n1. Exact primary-gauge changes and completion follow n1/G331. For decreasing continuous obstacles the actual D-envelope rule in n1 gives upper semicontinuous completed envelopes, including poles and bottom. No O(1/m) canonical rate or canonical FG for general surface model obstacles is claimed. A rational d yields a rational maximal coefficient vector by finite rational linear programming, but this does not identify its nef line bundle with a single ideal profile or prove semiampleness.

There is an explicit mixed-characteristic and positive-characteristic diagnostic instance. For a two-dimensional excellent regular local ring with parameters x,y and residue field k, blow up m=(x,y) and then the k-rational point y/x=0 of its exceptional curve. The affine point-blowup charts are regular: at a point of the exceptional curve their maximal ideals have the expected two generators and dimension two. The strict first curve E_1 and second curve E_2 have degree matrix Q=[[-2,1],[1,-1]]: the first self-degree decreases by one from -1, the new exceptional has degree -1, and their transverse intersection has length one. Pullback E_m=E_1+E_2. The negative of 2E_1+3E_2 has strictly positive degrees on both curves. Stacks33.44.15 on the full closed fibre and30.21.4 over the local base, both with complete immediate proofs read, make it relatively ample. The primary presentation argument in Step1 then realizes this very two-blowup surface as an actual primary model after an ample power. For obstacle D=-E_1-3E_2, the greatest feasible vector is (-3/2,-3), with Qz*=(0,3/2). The ideal I=(x^2,y) becomes generated with divisor E_1+2E_2 on these two blowups: in the x chart it is x(x,y/x), whose second blowup principalizes the residual maximal ideal; at the other centres it is already invertible. Therefore the exact envelope is -3v(I)/2. This example is valid for k[[x,y]] in every characteristic and for Z_p[[u]] with x=p,y=u; the latter is a complete excellent regular surface of mixed characteristic. It involves no Frobenius or characteristic-zero BFJ citation.

Own tiny exact program surface_checks.py reports PASS on all225 coefficient obstacles d_i=i/2, -10<=i<=4, for this two-curve matrix, and all925 pairs of their feasible vertices under coordinatewise maximum. It gives the example vector (-3/2,-3) and degrees (0,3/2). This is exhaustive finite rational linear-algebra evidence ONLY; it computes no ideals or semivaluations and does not prove the universal surface theorem. The universal proofs are Steps1--4 above.

The original general excellent task remains open in higher dimension and for unrestricted nonnormal conductor envelope descent.
